name: Cost-ordered model tier selector with outage and allowance recovery
description: Starts each piece of work on the cheapest rung its difficulty allows and tracks new releases by family name, so the choice improves when a new model ships without an edit.
purpose: Choose the model rung that starts each piece of work, and resume work after a provider outage or usage limit rather than failing it.
approach: Start each piece of work on the rung its difficulty calls for, and step down a tier when that tier is exhausted.
out_of_scope: Judging whether the cheapest model still succeeded, which needs live runs.
milestones: 1. Tier-selection cases passed by the live rule: 42 of 42, with a pin always winning and an exhausted tier falling to the next cheaper one. [met: 2026-10-22]
knowledge: The planner already rates difficulty on the call that decides the route, so starting-model choice costs no extra model call. Past incidents: queued tasks failed outright when a provider briefly overloaded and had to be rerun by hand, and a subscription allowance limit looks like a failed run rather than an outage, so each needs its own recognition and a resume time.
measures_of_success: Each difficulty maps to the stated starting rung, family names track new releases without edits, a pin always wins, an exhausted tier falls to the next cheaper one, and outages and limits are recognised with a correct resume time.
parameters: A difficulty rating, a ladder of rungs, optional operator model mapping and pins, a tier or family name, the list of live models, and the current time for limit parsing.
inputs: The planner's difficulty rating, a provider's live model list, error or result text from a failed model call, and the clock.
outputs: A starting model and ladder, a concrete model id for a tier or family, the next lower tier, a vision-capability answer, an outage verdict, and a usage-limit record with its reset and resume times.
effects: Remembers the latest outage and usage limit lane-wide, optionally persisted to a file, so other tasks hold off until the resume time.
usage_notes: Resolve names through the registry at the point of use rather than pinning release ids; set an operator pin only when a specific model is required. Treat an outage as a reason to requeue, not to fail the task.
